items.gist: Hearing brahmavidyā at death liberates the being through prior saṃskāra; all this is the stated truth.
Those lacking this knowledge offer conflicting accounts; the teaching from Śrī Śambhunātha destroys fear of death.
Even worldly festivals produce joy like waves of consciousness; special deity worship is prescribed on such days.
The two kinds of yoginī gathering yield knowledge; in melaka, consciousness expands without jealousy or contraction.
Heterogeneous elements should not be introduced into consciousness; after entry one should not be examined, and circle worship is repeated.
Gurus are distinguished by scriptural knowledge; the Devīyāmala lists ten Śiva-natured gurus with differing internal functions.
The disciple requests exposition with worship; the compassionate guru teaches even the lowly, considering possible śaktipāta.
The ritual seat, deities, and circle are worshipped with offerings before exposition begins.
The guru expounds by connecting sūtra, word, sentence, and chapter, using nyāya and adapting to the disciple's capacity.
After finishing a topic, one performs tarpaṇa and worship; special worship and niṣkṛti are prescribed for lapses.
Prāyaścitta is taught for those not knowing truth; mixing practices causes loss of knowledge, so it must be avoided.
Specific expiations are given for serious faults, including śivahasta recitation and mālinī/mātṛkā japa for various crimes.
